description: Deliver the Owner-only Slack DM vertical for a Mohist Agent: install a stateless mohist-slack adapter, create/configure/claim a Connection, dispatch one DM task through the Agent API, and receive the result in the same conversation — with provider inbox/outbox reliability, encrypted credentials, and the four independent Connection facts (Setup/Desired/health/Readiness) never collapsed.

tasks.title: Encrypted credential secret store
tasks.spec: specs/slack-connection-setup/spec.md#Credentials are entered and stored only through protected channels
tasks.description: Introduce the repo's first encryption primitive: an `ISecretStore` abstraction backed by `AesGcmSecretStore` (`System.Security.Cryptography.AesGCM`) with a master key file at `MOHIST_SECRET_KEY_PATH` / `~/.mohist/slack-master.key` (32 random bytes, `0600`, non-symlink, auto-generated, mirroring `OperatorCredential`'s file discipline). Ciphertext blobs (nonce + tag + ciphertext) persist in a new `ConnectionSecrets` table keyed by `(ConnectionId, Kind ∈ {appToken, botToken})` via an EF migration. This is the seam later features (Runner creds, webhook secrets) reuse.
acceptanceCriteria: ISecretStore exposes Store/Load/Delete; AesGcmSecretStore round-trips plaintext and fails cleanly on a wrong/missing master key.
The master key file is auto-created with 0600 (non-Windows), symlinks are rejected, and a world-readable file is refused on load.
Stored tokens never appear in logs, transcripts, or config reads (redaction mirrors ConfigRoutes.cs:99-104 for any *token field).
The ConnectionSecrets EF migration applies cleanly on top of the current schema.
Server tests cover round-trip, wrong-key failure, file-permission/symlink rejection, and delete using in-memory SQLite with fakes only; npm test passes.
tasks.output: ISecretStore + AesGcmSecretStore + master key file discipline + ConnectionSecrets table and EF migration.
tasks.notes: Implements design D2. This task delivers only the encrypted secret-store seam (no Connection consumer yet); T-003 and T-007 consume it. Closes the spec's '由 Server 加密保存' gap (slack-agent-connection.md:134) that the existing plaintext OperatorCredential does not satisfy.

tasks.title: AgentConnection aggregate and lifecycle
tasks.spec: specs/agent-connection/spec.md#A Connection binds one Agent, one workspace, and one Bot identity immutably
tasks.description: Add the AgentConnection aggregate in the Agent domain: a column-per-field `AgentConnection` domain + `AgentConnectionRow` + scoped `AgentConnectionStore` + `AgentQuerier` (mirroring RoutingRule/WatchEntry, not a grain). Binding (`AgentId, WorkspaceTeamId, AppId, BotUserId`) is immutable after create; the four independent facts (`SetupProgress, DesiredState, ConnectionHealth, AgentReadiness`) are real queryable columns; `OwnerSlackUserId` is set by claim. DbContext config adds a unique index on `(ProjectId, AgentId, WorkspaceTeamId)` where `DeletedAt IS NULL` (at most one non-deleted Connection per Agent+workspace). Deliver create/list/view/edit/delete; deletion cascades provider records but preserves the Agent and accepted work.
acceptanceCriteria: create binds one active Agent + one workspace + one Bot identity immutably; an archived Agent is rejected and no Connection is created.
A second non-deleted Connection for the same (Project, Agent, workspace) is refused without overwriting the existing one; distinct workspaces allow coexistence.
The Connection stores no Instructions/Runtime/Model/Skills/concurrency — only binding, access policy, lifecycle, and the four facts.

SetupProgress, DesiredState, ConnectionHealth, and AgentReadiness persist and read as four independent facts; none collapses into a single Connected value (a healthy Connection with a not-ready Agent reads as such).
delete removes provider integration records (credentials/inbox/mapping/outbox) but preserves the Agent, its Jobs, Sessions, and accepted inputs; the Agent remains launchable from Web/CLI unchanged.
Server spec tests cover binding/immutability/uniqueness/four-fact-independence/deletion using migrated in-memory SQLite + fakes; npm test passes.
tasks.output: AgentConnection domain + AgentConnectionRow + AgentConnectionStore + AgentQuerier + DbContext mapping + unique index + create/list/view/edit/delete + EF migration.
tasks.notes: Implements design D1. Follows the RoutingRule/WatchEntry column-per-field pattern (MohistDbContext.cs:399-440), not the Agent JSON-blob pattern, because binding and the four facts must be individually indexed/queryable and (Agent,workspace) uniqueness needs real columns. Credentials/inbox/outbox are separate Server-infrastructure aggregates keyed by ConnectionId (T-001, T-004).

tasks.title: Slack API client and Setup identity verification
tasks.spec: specs/slack-connection-setup/spec.md#Identity is verified before owner claim becomes available
tasks.description: Add `ISlackApiClient` as a typed HttpClient (auth.test, bots.info, users.info, conversations.info, users.list) registered via `AddHttpClient<ISlackApiClient, SlackApiClient>()` with a recording fake (mirroring IHermesWebhookClient). Implement Setup identity verification: load the Bot token via ISecretStore, call auth.test/bots.info/conversations.info, verify workspace/App/Bot consistency and required scopes, and drive the SetupProgress state machine — CreateAppCredentials → WaitingForSlackService when the adapter is offline → FixSlackSetup on token invalid / App-Bot mismatch / missing scope → ClaimOwner on success. Completed steps are preserved across adapter offline, token invalid, or Agent-not-ready.
acceptanceCriteria: ISlackApiClient is registered as a typed HttpClient with a recording fake usable by tests.

Verification advances SetupProgress to ClaimOwner only when workspace/App/Bot are consistent and required scopes are present; any inconsistency yields FixSlackSetup with a confirmed, actionable reason.
When mohist-slack is offline, the Connection stays in WaitingForSlackService and retains saved credentials and prior confirmed steps.

When a fresh adapter heartbeat is recorded (a successful /adapter-session call), SetupProgress can advance past Waiting for Slack service; a stale heartbeat (against injectable TimeProvider) reads as adapter-offline independently of stored Setup progress.
Verification loads the Bot token via ISecretStore and never logs it; SetupProgress advances independently of Agent Readiness.
A Connection whose identity cannot be verified does not present the claim action and never invites a user to wait for an unreceivable DM.
Server tests use a fake ISlackApiClient and injectable TimeProvider with no real network; npm test passes.
tasks.output: ISlackApiClient + SlackApiClient + recording fake; Setup identity verification driving the SetupProgress state machine.
tasks.notes: Implements design D3 (Server-side read/verify half). The Server is the identity authority; the adapter (T-009) only owns event/message transport and never makes identity/access decisions.

tasks.title: Provider inbox and outbound outbox
tasks.spec: specs/slack-provider-reliability/spec.md#The provider inbox deduplicates by stable Slack message identity and is bounded
tasks.description: Add Server-infrastructure provider reliability (keyed by ConnectionId, outside Agent/Session domains): `SlackProviderInboxStore` + `SlackProviderInboxRow` with a unique index on `(ConnectionId, SlackMessageIdentity)` for dedup-on-insert (InboxStore precedent) and bounded per-connection capacity (refuse on overflow, never evict accepted); and `SlackOutboxStore` + `SlackOutboxRow` with Kind {ReplaceableProgress, TerminalResult, ExplicitFailure, UserAction} and State {Pending, Claimed, Delivered, DeliveryUncertain, DeadLettered}, where replaceable progress is merged to the latest before claim and terminal/failure/user-action rows are never silently dropped. Add a cluster-singleton `slack-outbox-dispatcher` Orleans reminder (EventDispatcherGrain precedent) with backoff retry + dead-letter (IDeadLetterStore) + Delivery uncertain surfacing. Overflow flips ConnectionHealth to Degraded(Backpressured) and stops ingress. Survive adapter/Server restart; never override AgentJob/AgentTurn result authority.
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate Slack message identity resolves to one inbox entry and produces no second SessionInput; capacity overflow refuses new ingress without dropping any accepted event.
Replaceable progress entries are merged to the latest; terminal results, explicit failures, and user-action messages are never silently dropped.
Outbox overflow moves ConnectionHealth to Degraded(Backpressured), stops accepting new Slack input, and lets already-accepted execution continue under Mohist authority.
Unconfirmed delivery is reported as Delivery uncertain and is not blindly reduplicated; manual resend warns of possible duplication.
After adapter or Server restart, accepted inbox events remain accepted and unsent outbox entries remain pending (no loss or duplication from the restart).
Slack delivery success or failure never changes an AgentJob or AgentTurn result; the Server remains the sole result authority.
Server tests use fake storage and injectable TimeProvider for backoff/retry, no real network; npm test passes.
tasks.output: SlackProviderInboxStore/Row + SlackOutboxStore/Row + slack-outbox-dispatcher reminder + dead-letter integration + Backpressured/Delivery-uncertain surfacing + EF migration.
tasks.notes: Implements design D6. Reuses the InboxStore dedup-on-insert idiom and the EventDispatcherGrain + IDeadLetterStore delivery idiom so the repo keeps one reliability pattern. Inbox (protects Server) and outbox (protects Slack / Backpressured) are split because ingress and egress have different capacity, ordering, and failure semantics.

tasks.title: Owner claim flow
tasks.spec: specs/slack-connection-setup/spec.md#Owner claim uses a short-lived single-use code validated against workspace membership
tasks.description: Implement owner claim: `claim-owner` generates a short-lived (default 10 min, injectable TimeProvider) single-use code and stores only its hash + expiry + UsedAt; regeneration supersedes and immediately invalidates any prior code. On an inbound DM claim envelope, look up the unused+unexpired code, call users.info via ISlackApiClient, and accept the claim only if the sender is a current regular (non-guest, non-bot, non-deactivated) member of the bound workspace and of no other workspace; on success set OwnerSlackUserId, advance SetupProgress to Complete, and mark the code used. After claim, DM access is owner-only: a non-owner DM is rejected and creates no Agent resources.
acceptanceCriteria: The claim code is stored hashed (not plaintext); an expired, used, or superseded code is rejected.
Regenerating a code immediately invalidates the prior code.
Only a current regular workspace member can claim; guests, bots, deactivated members, and members of other workspaces are rejected and establish no Owner.
A successful claim establishes exactly one Owner and advances SetupProgress to Complete.
After claim, a non-owner DM is rejected with an explicit denial and creates no AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, AgentTurn, or inbox entry.
Server tests use a fake ISlackApiClient and injectable TimeProvider for code expiry; npm test passes.
tasks.output: Hashed single-use claim code generation/validation + users.info membership check + Owner establishment + owner-only DM gating.
tasks.notes: Implements design D7. The code is a single-use ownership bearer, not a credential. Membership is validated Server-side via users.info (D3), never by display name/message text and never delegated to the adapter.

tasks.title: Connection dispatch through the Agent API
tasks.spec: specs/slack-dm-dispatch/spec.md#A DM task dispatches one launch through the Agent API
tasks.description: Add `IAgentLauncher.LaunchConnectionAsync(agent, prompt, ConnectionLaunchOrigin)` reusing the origin-in-key encoding pattern shared by the routed/mention launch paths; derive the idempotency key as `KeyFor(projectId, "slack:{teamId}:{conversationId}:{messageTs}")` and route through `AgentLaunchCoordinatorGrain` exactly like the manual `LaunchIdempotentAsync` path so redelivery collapses to the same plan; stamp `source-kind=agent-connection` plus connection-id/slack-user-id/slack-conversation-id audit labels on the Session; carry a ConnectionOrigin field through the existing coordinator envelope (no new coordinator grain). Add the adapter HTTP routes authenticated by the operator token: POST .../ingress (single inbound route — durable inbox write before ack, then server-side classification: reject if Setup not Complete, process claim if text matches a pending code, reject if sender is not Owner, otherwise call LaunchConnectionAsync and reply accepted/queued/rejected), POST .../adapter-session (credential lease + heartbeat, returns decrypted App/Bot tokens and records LastHeartbeatAt), and POST .../deliveries/claim + /ack (outbox drain). Redelivery resolves to the same SessionInput; the final result returns to the same DM conversation via the outbox. This issue dispatches one task per DM with no continuation semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: One owner DM task creates exactly one AgentJob, one AgentSession, one first SessionInput, and one first AgentTurn via LaunchConnectionAsync; the idempotency key is derived from (team, conversation, messageTs).
Slack redelivery of the same message — including after adapter or Server restart — resolves to the same SessionInput and creates no second job, input, or turn.
A bare mention without a task creates no work and the Bot asks the Owner to supply a task; the Bot replies accepted, queued, or an explicit rejection with an actionable reason.
The terminal result is delivered to the same DM conversation; an unconfirmable result is surfaced honestly rather than fabricated.
A second DM task dispatches an independent launch; this issue makes no continuation, queue-merge, or current-Session commitment.

The /ingress route classifies server-side and the adapter does not pre-classify: a DM dispatched before Setup is Complete is rejected with no Agent resources; a non-owner DM is rejected with no resources; a DM whose text matches a pending claim code is processed as a claim, not a task.
The /adapter-session route authenticates the adapter, returns the decrypted App/Bot tokens, and records the Connection heartbeat; tokens never appear in logs.
Adapter routes are authenticated by the operator token and resolve the Connection before any dispatch.
Server tests use fake dispatch, fake storage, and injectable TimeProvider with no real network; npm test passes.
tasks.output: LaunchConnectionAsync (coordinator-routed) + source-kind=agent-connection labels + coordinator ConnectionOrigin + ingress (classifying) / adapter-session (lease+heartbeat) / deliveries HTTP routes.
tasks.notes: Implements design D4 + D5. LaunchConnectionAsync routes through AgentLaunchCoordinatorGrain (like LaunchIdempotentAsync) — the connection-derived key IS the coordinator idempotency key, which is what makes a redelivered Slack message resolve to the same SessionInput (#512 inherited). The origin-in-key encoding pattern is shared with the routed/mention paths (IAgentLauncher.cs:98, 119); it does not reuse those methods' call paths. Dispatch is internal to the /ingress handler (server-side classification); there is no separate adapter-facing dispatch route. source-kind=agent-connection distinguishes Slack sessions for audit and for the later DM-conversation feature.

tasks.title: CLI connection command group
tasks.spec: specs/slack-connection-setup/spec.md#A CLI connection subgroup manages the Connection lifecycle
tasks.description: Add the `mo agent connection` subgroup: create/configure/claim-owner/view/list/edit/delete (rotate-credentials/transfer-owner/enable/disable are deliberately absent). `create` outputs the Connection id, Slack identity preview, and prefilled Create-in-Slack reference without requiring the adapter online. `configure` reads credentials via hidden terminal input or `--credentials-file` (UTF-8 JSON {appToken,botToken}, validated 0600 + non-symlink), and refuses command-line token arguments. `claim-owner` generates and prints the one-time code once. Commands target the T-002/T-003/T-005 server endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: create, configure, claim-owner, view, list, edit, delete are present; rotate-credentials, transfer-owner, enable, and disable are absent.
`create` succeeds without the adapter online and outputs the Connection identity and prefilled Slack reference.
`configure` reads hidden input or a protected credentials file, refuses command-line token args, and refuses a symlink or world-readable file; credentials are never echoed or logged.
`claim-owner` prints the one-time code once; regenerating invalidates the prior code.
CLI tests cover each command and the credential-input validation paths; npm test passes.
tasks.output: mo agent connection subgroup (create/configure/claim-owner/view/list/edit/delete) with protected credential input.
tasks.notes: Implements design D8 (CLI command half). Web and CLI configure the same Connection record — there is no second local config. Credential-file discipline mirrors OperatorCredential (0600 + non-symlink).

tasks.title: Minimal Agent Readiness derivation
tasks.spec: specs/agent-connection/spec.md#Readiness gaps produce honest dispatch decisions
tasks.description: Add a minimal Server-side config-derived Agent Readiness on the Connection read surface: NeedsSetup if AgentConfig is null or lacks model+runtime; Ready if both are present; Unknown as the default. Integrate into dispatch decisions (T-006): NeedsSetup rejects a new dispatch with an actionable reason while the Connection stays healthy; Unknown accepts and awaits Runner verification; Ready accepts. Show Readiness independently of ConnectionHealth on the four-facts surface.
acceptanceCriteria: Readiness is derived from AgentConfig as NeedsSetup/Ready/Unknown, with Unknown as the default for any un-probed Agent.
A NeedsSetup Agent rejects a new DM dispatch with an actionable reason while the Connection remains healthy; an Unknown Agent accepts and awaits Runner verification; a Ready Agent accepts.
Readiness is shown independently of ConnectionHealth (no single Connected collapse; a healthy Connection with a not-ready Agent reads as such).
Server tests cover all three dispatch decisions and the independent display; npm test passes.
The docs/agents.md Readiness gap note is updated to describe this minimal derivation and flag the full probe as a follow-up.
tasks.output: Config-derived Agent Readiness (NeedsSetup/Ready/Unknown) on the Connection surface + dispatch-decision integration.
tasks.notes: Implements design D9. Deliberately minimal — a real Runner/runtime Readiness probe is a follow-up (Open Questions). Unknown-as-default avoids falsely claiming any configured Agent is Ready; the authoritative AgentJob/Turn result still governs the actual outcome regardless of the Readiness label.

tasks.title: mohist-slack adapter package
tasks.spec: specs/mohist-slack-adapter/spec.md#The adapter is a stateless protocol translator
tasks.description: Add `packages/mohist-slack/` as a new npm workspace package (append to root workspaces) using `@slack/socket-mode` + `@slack/web-api`. Implement: Socket Mode connect, normalize events to envelopes with a stable provider identity, call POST .../adapter-session on start and on a short interval (credential lease + heartbeat), forward every normalized event to the single POST .../ingress route (the adapter does not pre-classify owner/claim/non-owner), drain the outbox via deliveries/claim+ack, render and post replies via chat.postMessage, report delivery results, hold leased tokens in memory only, apply an in-flight concurrency cap, and hold no durable state. Authenticate to the Server with the operator token. Include an end-to-end fake round-trip against the T-006 routes.
acceptanceCriteria: The package is added to root workspaces and builds a dist/cli.js; root build/test include it.
The adapter connects Socket Mode, normalizes events to envelopes, and forwards every event to /ingress without classifying it; it does not call a separate dispatch route.
The adapter calls /adapter-session on start and on a short interval to lease tokens and record its heartbeat; tokens are held in memory only and never persisted.
The adapter drains the outbox via claim/ack and posts replies via chat.postMessage.
The adapter persists no inbox/mapping/pending/Agent-config state; reconnect re-leases tokens, re-heartbeats, and resumes pulling unconverged items from the Server.
The adapter bounds its in-flight concurrency and does not own a persistent queue or apply product-level backpressure (the Server decides Backpressured).
The adapter reaches execution only through the Connection boundary and does not call mo, the database, grains, Runner, or Runtime protocols directly.
One adapter carries multiple Connections, each with independent App/Bot credentials.

mohist-slack tests use a fake Slack (event ingress/ack/redelivery/member directory) and a fake Server transport with no real Slack/network; npm run typecheck -w packages/mohist-slack, npm test -w packages/mohist-slack, and npm test pass.
tasks.output: packages/mohist-slack workspace package: Socket Mode client + envelope normalization + single ingress forward + adapter-session lease/heartbeat + delivery-drain + reply posting + concurrency cap.
tasks.notes: Implements design D8 (adapter half) and honors architecture.md:49 (Slack protocol in mohist-slack) + :233-234 (stateless; anything that must survive restart lives in Server). Using the official @slack SDKs avoids hand-rolling the Socket Mode WebSocket protocol (design D8 alternative rejected).

tasks.title: CLI Slack service management
tasks.description: Add Slack as a first-class CLI service target: ServiceTarget.Slack, IServiceInstaller.InstallSlackAsync + six lifecycle methods + IsSlackInstalledAsync, a `mohist-slack.service` systemd unit in SystemdServiceInstaller (ExecStart = node packages/mohist-slack/dist/cli.js, Restart=on-failure, env SERVER_URL + operator token) mirroring the runner unit, and the WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller equivalent. Deliver mo install slack, mo service status|start|stop|restart|logs slack, and mo update slack.
acceptanceCriteria: ServiceTarget.Slack is present; mo install slack installs the mohist-slack.service unit.
mo service status slack reports whether mohist-slack is installed and running; start/stop/restart/logs/uninstall operate on the slack unit.
The unit ExecStart points at the T-009 package dist/cli.js and carries the SERVER_URL + operator-token environment.
CLI tests cover install and the lifecycle verbs using a fake installer; npm test passes.
The docs/self-host.md gap notes for mo install slack / mo service status slack / mo update slack are updated to reflect the now-implemented surface.
tasks.output: ServiceTarget.Slack + IServiceInstaller slack methods + systemd/scheduled-task units + mo install/status/update slack verbs.
tasks.notes: Implements design D8 (CLI service half). Mirrors the runner unit (SystemdServiceInstaller.cs:53-69): Linux = systemctl --user, Windows = schtasks. The unit can only start once T-009's dist/cli.js exists.
